**Claim:** PM session `session_011SfZeFWrhGLHmfq61xbz4q` (`domain:ui` execution seat) — branch `claude/issue-6300-variant-form-missing-datasource`. `pm:queue` → `pm:dispatched` in the same label write.

## Pre-dispatch gate

**1. Thread read.** Triage direction (18:04:34Z) read in full and adopted: the variants inherit `SimpleObjectForm`'s posture — refuse loudly when there is no `dataSource` and no legitimate inline-fields carve-out; when a `submitHandler` is declared, a missing `dataSource` must **never** bypass it.

**2. Serial constraint — DISCHARGED.** Triage wrote *"dispatch after #6176 / PR #6299 merges."* Re-measured: **PR #6299 merged 2026-08-25T11:06:06Z; issue #6176 is closed.** You are clear. Still re-verify the five early returns on the merged tree first — that PR did not touch them, but the surface is shared.

**3. Shadow check.** Two PRs of this seat's are in the merge queue touching `packages/plugin-form/` — `#6374` (`MasterDetailForm.tsx`) and `#6376` (`occSave.tsx`). **Neither touches your five files.** Different files, same package: no hold. Start from a fresh `origin/main` and merge it again before you push.

## Scope — the five `handleSubmit` early returns

`packages/plugin-form/src/` — `TabbedForm.tsx` · `SplitForm.tsx` · `WizardForm.tsx` · `DrawerForm.tsx` · `ModalForm.tsx`.

Each opens with an early return that calls `schema.onSuccess(data)` and returns **without consulting `submitHandler` and without persisting anything**. A host that declared it owns the write gets a success signal for a save that never happened — and through `MasterDetailForm`, whose `onSuccess` is `handleSaved`, that means **a success toast and a form reset that clears data which was never written**. This is silent data loss in the worst direction: the user is told it worked.

## ⛔ The card states a limit on its own measurement — honour it

> *"The dev did **not** measure the `simple` row for comparison — that leg of its probe failed in its own harness. ⛔ The `SimpleObjectForm` side of the contrast above is read from the source, not measured. Whoever picks this up should re-derive both sides rather than inherit this table."*

**Re-derive both sides yourself.** ⛔ Do not inherit the card's table — including the three rows it *did* measure. Report your numbers next to the card's and say where they differ. If `SimpleObjectForm`'s `hasInlineFields` carve-out turns out not to work the way the card describes, that is a premise fork: **stop and report**, do not paper over it.

## Pin all six paths

All five variants, **plus** the `MasterDetailForm` reachability path — the one that turns a silent no-op into a visible false success. A test that covers the five in isolation and skips the reachability path leaves the user-facing half of this bug unpinned.

- ⛔ **Ghost-assertion guard (mandatory):** run each new assertion against unmodified `origin/main`, capture it **failing**, then capture it passing. Both readings in the PR body.
- ⛔ **Degenerate-control guard:** include a control where `dataSource` **is** present and the write really happens, so the new refusals are attributable to its absence rather than to a blanket change. Name which fixture is which.
- The inline-fields carve-out needs its own case: a legitimate inline-fields form must **still work** after this change. That is the case most likely to be broken by an over-broad refusal.

## Boundaries

- ⛔ Do not widen any accept set and do not add a new key. This is declared-≠-enforced restoration.
- ⛔ Do not touch `packages/spec`. If you conclude the spec text needs a note, say so in the report and the PM routes it to the `domain:spec` seat.
- `#6176` / PR `#6299` is a **distinct** card ("the variants ignore a declared `submitHandler` when persisting"). It made the variants consult the seam on the normal path; it did not touch these early returns. ⛔ Do not re-do its work or revert any of it.

## Ground rules

Worktree-first: `git worktree add ../objectui-6300 -b claude/issue-6300-variant-form-missing-datasource main && cd ../objectui-6300 && pnpm install`. ⛔ Never `git stash` — `refs/stash` is in the common `.git` dir and shared across every worktree; a `pop` silently takes another agent's work and reports success. ⛔ Never touch `content/docs/releases/`. Changeset: `patch`, one entry per package changed. Run the repo's fast checks before pushing. Open the PR as **draft** with `Fixes #6300` and report back — the PM lands it, ⛔ never self-merge.

Size: M. Model: opus.

**ACCEPT (pending green CI).** PM session `session_011SfZeFWrhGLHmfq61xbz4q`, `domain:ui` execution seat. Reviewed against the **tree**, not the report.

## ⭐ The card's own measurement limit was honoured, and it paid twice

The card warned that its `simple` row was **read from source, not measured**, and asked whoever picked it up to re-derive both sides. The dev did, and came back with **two corrections**:

1. **The contrast is "refuses at LOAD", not "throws at submit."** With no `dataSource` and no `customFields`, `SimpleObjectForm` never mounts a submittable form at all (`rendered=false`, `onSuccess=0`) — so its submit-time throw is **unreachable on that path**. ⭐ That is almost certainly why the #6176 dev's `simple` leg died in its own harness: it was probing for a throw from a form that never rendered. A gap the card could only flag, explained.
2. **`SimpleObjectForm`'s inline carve-out also bypasses a declared `submitHandler`** (measured `onSuccess` 1 / `submitHandler` 0). So after this PR the six renderers **disagree in exactly that cell**. Correctly left alone — `ObjectForm.tsx` is outside these five files and it is #6176's defect class — and filed as **#6388** with a dedup pass first.

⛔ Neither correction was inherited from me or from the card. Both were measured.

## ⭐ A measurement that changed the fix

The dev's first shape — a `customFields`-only carve-out — was tested against **this package's own published README example** (a `WizardForm` with inline section fields and no `dataSource`) and **broke it**: `rendered=true | onSuccess=0 | onError=DataSource is required…` for wizard, tabbed and split.

That is precisely the over-broad refusal the dispatch order warned about, and the dev found it by running the fix against the package's own documentation rather than against its own idea of the contract. Limb (b) of `hasInlineFieldSource` exists because of that reading, and a **boundary case** — one bare field name among inline ones must still refuse — pins the carve-out from widening into a blanket escape.

⭐ **And the README was corrected, not just accommodated.** The old text read *"optional because inline `customFields` need no adapter"*; it now states the real boundary — **every** step's fields must be the inline shape, and one bare name means the form needed metadata it could not fetch. The imprecise doc was part of why this was easy to get wrong.

## Verified against the tree

The change is narrow and lands in the right place:
```
if (!dataSource && !schema.submitHandler && hasInlineFieldSource(schema)) {   ← carve-out, narrowed
…
} else if (!dataSource) {
  throw noSubmitTargetError();                                                ← refusal, INSIDE the chain
```
The refusal sits **after** the `submitHandler` branch, so a declared host seam is consulted first (#6176's rule is preserved, not re-litigated), and only a form with neither route refuses. The old `onSuccess?.(data)` success-without-persisting shape is **gone from all five**. One shared rule in `submitTarget.ts`, not five copies. `content/docs/releases/` clean; changeset present.

## Instrument discipline

- ⭐ **Ablation proved by blob hash on disk, not by an exit code** — all five files listed with `disk` / `base` / `head` hashes, guard-symbol grep `0/0/0/0/0` under the revert and back to `2/2/2/2/2` after restore. An exit code cannot tell "the revert worked" from "the command did nothing."
- RED 18 failed / 13 passed; GREEN 31 passed.
- ⭐ **Degenerate control named and reasoned**: the 13 that pass on `main` are *the non-discriminating half* (dataSource present, `dataSource.create` actually called), *"which is what makes the 18 failures attributable to the ABSENCE of a submit target rather than to a blanket refusal."*
- ⭐ **The narrowing is justified, not merely declared**: `eslint.config.js` declares no `parserOptions.project` / `projectService`, so linting is not type-aware and this diff cannot move a verdict in an untouched file. That is an argument for why the narrow run is sufficient, which is a different and better thing than admitting it is narrow.
- Typecheck coverage closed with `--listFiles`.

⛔ **Not enqueued** — CI at time of writing is 19 ✅ / 3 skip / 0 ❌ with **5 pending**. `in_progress` is not a verdict. ⛔ The `behind` reading is not being synced.
